          - heading [level=2] [ref=f2e458]:
            - link "Attributes" [ref=f2e459] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#attributes"
          - paragraph [ref=f2e460]:
            - text: The
            - code [ref=f2e461]: <input>
            - text: element is so powerful because of its attributes; the
            - link [ref=f2e462] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#type"
              - code [ref=f2e463]: type
            - text: attribute, described with examples above, being the most important. Since every
            - code [ref=f2e464]: <input>
            - text: element, regardless of type, is based on the
            - link [ref=f2e465] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLInputElement
              - code [ref=f2e466]: HTMLInputElement
            - text: interface, they technically share the exact same set of attributes. However, in reality, most attributes have an effect on only a specific subset of input types. In addition, the way some attributes impact an input depends on the input type, impacting different input types in different ways.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e467]: This section provides a table listing all the attributes with a brief description. This table is followed by a list describing each attribute in greater detail, along with which input types they are associated with. Those that are common to most or all input types are defined in greater detail below. Attributes that are unique to particular input types—or attributes which are common to all input types but have special behaviors when used on a given input type—are instead documented on those types' pages.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e468]:
            - text: Attributes for the
            - code [ref=f2e469]: <input>

            - link "global HTML attributes" [ref=f2e470] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes
            - text: "and additionally:"

            - definition [ref=f2e895]:
              - paragraph [ref=f2e896]:
                - text: A Boolean attribute which, if present, indicates that the input should automatically have focus when the page has finished loading (or when the
                - link [ref=f2e897] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog
                  - code [ref=f2e898]: <dialog>
                - text: containing the element has been displayed).
              - paragraph [ref=f2e900]:
                - strong [ref=f2e901]: "Note:"
                - text: An element with the
                - code [ref=f2e902]: autofocus
                - text: attribute may gain focus before the
                - link [ref=f2e903] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event
                  - code [ref=f2e904]: DOMContentLoaded
                - text: event is fired.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e905]:
                - text: No more than one element in the document may have the
                - code [ref=f2e906]: autofocus
                - text: attribute. If put on more than one element, the first one with the attribute receives focus.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e907]:
                - text: The
                - code [ref=f2e908]: autofocus
                - text: attribute cannot be used on inputs of type
                - code [ref=f2e909]: hidden
                - text: ", since hidden inputs cannot be focused."
              - paragraph [ref=f2e911]:
                - strong [ref=f2e912]: "Warning:"
                - text: Automatically focusing a form control can confuse visually-impaired people using screen-reading technology and people with cognitive impairments. When
                - code [ref=f2e913]: autofocus
                - text: is assigned, screen-readers "teleport" their user to the form control without warning them beforehand.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e914]:
                - text: Use careful consideration for accessibility when applying the
                - code [ref=f2e915]: autofocus
                - text: attribute. Automatically focusing on a control can cause the page to scroll on load. The focus can also cause dynamic keyboards to display on some touch devices. While a screen reader will announce the label of the form control receiving focus, the screen reader will not announce anything before the label, and the sighted user on a small device will equally miss the context created by the preceding content.

                - text: event, and disabled inputs are not submitted with the form.

                - code [ref=f2e1063]: <input>

                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Glossary/UTF-16
                - text: ) that the user can enter into the entry field. This must be a non-negative integer value smaller than or equal to the value specified by
                - code [ref=f2e1258]: maxlength
                - text: . If no
                - code [ref=f2e1259]: minlength
                - text: is specified, or an invalid value is specified, the input has no minimum length.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1260]:
                - text: The input will fail
                - link "constraint validation" [ref=f2e1261] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Guides/Constraint_validation
                - text: if the length of the text entered into the field is fewer than
                - code [ref=f2e1262]: minlength
                - link "UTF-16 code units" [ref=f2e1263] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Glossary/UTF-16
                - text: long, preventing form submission. Constraint validation is only applied when the value is changed by the user. See
                - link "Client-side validation" [ref=f2e1264] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#client-side_validation"
                - text: for more information.
            - term [ref=f2e1265]:
              - link [ref=f2e1266] [cursor=pointer]:

                - code [ref=f2e1267]: multiple
            - definition [ref=f2e1268]:
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1269]:
                - text: The Boolean

                - code [ref=f2e1271]: file

            - term [ref=f2e1274]:
              - link [ref=f2e1275] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: "#name"
                - code [ref=f2e1276]: name
            - definition [ref=f2e1277]:
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1278]: A string specifying a name for the input control. This name is submitted along with the control's value when the form data is submitted.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1279]:
                - text: Consider the
                - code [ref=f2e1280]: name
                - text: a required attribute (even though it's not). If an input has no
                - code [ref=f2e1281]: name
                - text: specified, or
                - code [ref=f2e1282]: name
                - text: is empty, the input's value is not submitted with the form! (Disabled controls, unchecked radio buttons, unchecked checkboxes, and reset buttons are also not sent.)
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1283]: "There are two special cases:"
              - list [ref=f2e1284]:
                - listitem [ref=f2e1285]:
                  - code [ref=f2e1286]: _charset_
                  - text: ": If used as the name of an"
                  - code [ref=f2e1287]: <input>
                  - text: element of type
                  - link "hidden" [ref=f2e1288] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/hidden
                  - text: ", the input's"
                  - code [ref=f2e1289]: value
                  - text: is automatically set by the
                  - link "user agent" [ref=f2e1290] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /en-US/docs/Glossary/User_agent
                  - text: to the character encoding being used to submit the form.
                - listitem [ref=f2e1291]:
                  - code [ref=f2e1292]: isindex
                  - text: ": For historical reasons, the name"
                  - link [ref=f2e1293] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fe-name
                    - code [ref=f2e1294]: isindex
                    - text: (external)
                  - text: is not allowed.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1295]:
                - text: The
                - link [ref=f2e1296] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#name"
                  - code [ref=f2e1297]: name
                - text: attribute creates a unique behavior for radio buttons.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1298]: Only one radio button in a same-named group of radio buttons can be checked at a time. Selecting any radio button in that group automatically deselects any currently-selected radio button in the same group. The value of that one checked radio button is sent along with the name if the form is submitted,
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1299]: When tabbing into a series of same-named group of radio buttons, if one is checked, that one will receive focus. If they aren't grouped together in source order, if one of the group is checked, tabbing into the group starts when the first one in the group is encountered, skipping all those that aren't checked. In other words, if one is checked, tabbing skips the unchecked radio buttons in the group. If none are checked, the radio button group receives focus when the first button in the same name group is reached.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1300]: Once one of the radio buttons in a group has focus, using the arrow keys will navigate through all the radio buttons of the same name, even if the radio buttons are not grouped together in the source order.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1301]:
                - text: When an input element is given a
                - code [ref=f2e1302]: name
                - text: ", that name becomes a property of the owning form element's"
                - link [ref=f2e1303] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLFormElement/elements
                  - code [ref=f2e1304]: HTMLFormElement.elements
                - text: property. If you have an input whose
                - code [ref=f2e1305]: name
                - text: is set to
                - code [ref=f2e1306]: guest
                - text: and another whose
                - code [ref=f2e1307]: name
                - text: is
                - code [ref=f2e1308]: hat-size
                - text: ", the following code can be used:"
              - generic [ref=f2e1310]:
                - generic [ref=f2e1311]:
                  - generic [ref=f2e1312]: js
                  - button "Copy" [ref=f2e1315] [cursor=pointer]
                - code [ref=f2e1318]: let form = document.querySelector("form"); let guestName = form.elements.guest; let hatSize = form.elements["hat-size"];
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1319]:
                - text: When this code has run,
                - code [ref=f2e1320]: guestName
                - text: will be the
                - link [ref=f2e1321] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLInputElement
                  - code [ref=f2e1322]: HTMLInputElement
                - text: for the
                - code [ref=f2e1323]: guest
                - text: field, and
                - code [ref=f2e1324]: hatSize
                - text: the object for the
                - code [ref=f2e1325]: hat-size
                - text: field.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1327]:
                - strong [ref=f2e1328]: "Warning:"
                - text: Avoid giving form elements a
                - code [ref=f2e1329]: name
                - text: that corresponds to a built-in property of the form, since you would then override the predefined property or method with this reference to the corresponding input.
            - term [ref=f2e1330]:
              - link [ref=f2e1331] [cursor=pointer]:
                - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/pattern
                - code [ref=f2e1332]: pattern
            - definition [ref=f2e1333]:
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1334]:
                - text: Valid for
                - code [ref=f2e1335]: text
                - text: ","
                - code [ref=f2e1336]: search
                - text: ","
                - code [ref=f2e1337]: url
                - text: ","
                - code [ref=f2e1338]: tel
                - text: ","
                - code [ref=f2e1339]: email
                - text: ", and"
                - code [ref=f2e1340]: password
                - text: ", the"
                - code [ref=f2e1341]: pattern
                - text: attribute is used to compile a regular expression that the input's
                - link [ref=f2e1342] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#value"
                  - code [ref=f2e1343]: value
                - text: must match in order for the value to pass
                - link "constraint validation" [ref=f2e1344] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Guides/Constraint_validation
                - text: . It must be a valid JavaScript regular expression, as used by the
                - link [ref=f2e1345] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/RegExp
                  - code [ref=f2e1346]: RegExp
                - text: type, and as documented in our
                - link "guide on regular expressions" [ref=f2e1347] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Regular_expressions
                - text: ". No forward slashes should be specified around the pattern text. When compiling the regular expression:"
              - list [ref=f2e1348]:
                - listitem [ref=f2e1349]:
                  - text: the pattern will be implicitly wrapped with
                  - code [ref=f2e1350]: "^(?:"
                  - text: and
                  - code [ref=f2e1351]: )$
                  - text: ", such that the match is required against the"
                  - emphasis [ref=f2e1352]: entire
                  - text: input value, i.e.,
                  - code [ref=f2e1353]: ^(?:<pattern>)$
                  - text: .
                - listitem [ref=f2e1354]:
                  - text: the
                  - code [ref=f2e1355]: "'v'"
                  - text: flag is specified so that the pattern is treated as a sequence of Unicode code points, instead of as
                  - link "ASCII" [ref=f2e1356] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /en-US/docs/Glossary/ASCII
                  - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1357]:
                - text: If the
                - code [ref=f2e1358]: pattern
                - text: attribute is present but is not specified or is invalid, no regular expression is applied and this attribute is ignored completely. If the pattern attribute is valid and a non-empty value does not match the pattern, constraint validation will prevent form submission. If the
                - link [ref=f2e1359] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/multiple
                  - code [ref=f2e1360]: multiple
                - text: is present, the compiled regular expression is matched against each comma separated value.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1362]:
                - strong [ref=f2e1363]: "Note:"
                - text: If using the
                - code [ref=f2e1364]: pattern
                - text: attribute, inform the user about the expected format by including explanatory text nearby. You can also include a
                - link [ref=f2e1365] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#title"
                  - code [ref=f2e1366]: title
                - text: attribute to explain what the requirements are to match the pattern; most browsers will display this title as a tooltip. The visible explanation is required for accessibility. The tooltip is an enhancement.

                - text: attribute provides a brief hint to the user as to what kind of information is expected in the field. It should be a word or short phrase that provides a hint as to the expected type of data, rather than an explanation or prompt. The text

                  - text: ","
                  - link [ref=f2e1538] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/month#step
                    - code [ref=f2e1539]: month
                  - text: ","
                  - link [ref=f2e1540] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/time#step
                    - code [ref=f2e1541]: time
                  - text: ", and"
                  - link [ref=f2e1542] [cursor=pointer]:
                    - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/week#step
                    - code [ref=f2e1543]: week
                  - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1544]:
                - text: The value must be a positive number—integer or float—or the special value
                - code [ref=f2e1545]: any
                - text: ", which means no stepping is implied, and any value is allowed (barring other constraints, such as"
                - link [ref=f2e1546] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/min
                  - code [ref=f2e1547]: min
                - text: and
                - link [ref=f2e1548] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/max
                  - code [ref=f2e1549]: max
                - text: ).
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1550]:
                - text: For example, if you have
                - code [ref=f2e1551]: <input type="number" min="10" step="2">
                - text: ", then any even integer,"
                - code [ref=f2e1552]: "10"
                - text: or greater, is valid. If omitted,
                - code [ref=f2e1553]: <input type="number">
                - text: ", any integer is valid, but floats (like"
                - code [ref=f2e1554]: "4.2"
                - text: ) are not valid, because
                - code [ref=f2e1555]: step
                - text: defaults to
                - code [ref=f2e1556]: "1"
                - text: . For
                - code [ref=f2e1557]: "4.2"
                - text: to be valid,
                - code [ref=f2e1558]: step
                - text: would have had to be set to
                - code [ref=f2e1559]: any
                - text: ", 0.1, 0.2, or the"
                - code [ref=f2e1560]: min
                - text: value would have had to be a number ending in
                - code [ref=f2e1561]: ".2"
                - text: ", such as"
                - code [ref=f2e1562]: <input type="number" min="-5.2">
                - text: .
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1564]:
                - strong [ref=f2e1565]: "Note:"
                - text: When the data entered by the user doesn't adhere to the stepping configuration, the value is considered invalid in constraint validation and will match the
                - code [ref=f2e1566]: :invalid
                - text: pseudoclass.
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1567]:
                - text: See
                - link "Client-side validation" [ref=f2e1568] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: "#client-side_validation"
                - text: for more information.

              - paragraph [ref=f2e1585]: Global attribute valid for all elements, including all the input types, an integer attribute indicating if the element can take input focus (is focusable), if it should participate to sequential keyboard navigation. As all input types except for input of type hidden are focusable, this attribute should not be used on form controls, because doing so would require the management of the focus order for all elements within the document with the risk of harming usability and accessibility if done incorrectly.

                - link "user agent" [ref=f2e1688] [cursor=pointer]:

                - link [ref=f2e1689] [cursor=pointer]:

                - text: object representing the search box. This allows your code to update the search results in real time as the user edits the search.

                - code [ref=f2e1694]: incremental

                - link [ref=f2e1695] [cursor=pointer]:
                  - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLInputElement/search_event
                  - code [ref=f2e1696]: search
                - text: event is only sent when the user explicitly initiates a search (such as by pressing the Enter or Return key while editing the field).
              - paragraph [ref=f2e1697]:
                - text: The
                - code [ref=f2e1698]: search
                - text: event is rate-limited so that it is not sent more frequently than an implementation-defined interval.

            - text: Labels are needed to associate assistive text with an
            - code [ref=f2e2106]: <input>

            - link [ref=f2e2107] [cursor=pointer]:

            - text: element provides explanatory information about a form field that is
            - emphasis [ref=f2e2109]: always
            - text: appropriate (aside from any layout concerns you have). It's never a bad idea to use a
            - code [ref=f2e2110]: <label>
            - text: to explain what should be entered into an
            - code [ref=f2e2111]: <input>

            - link [ref=f2e2112] [cursor=pointer]:

          - heading "Associated labels" [level=4] [ref=f2e2114]

            - code [ref=f2e2116]: <input>
            - text: and
            - code [ref=f2e2117]: <label>

              - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/label#for
              - code [ref=f2e2120]: for
            - text: attribute, you bond the label to the input in a way that lets screen readers describe inputs to users more precisely.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2121]:

            - text: "The first example is inaccessible: no relationship exists between the prompt and the"
            - code [ref=f2e2172]: <input>
            - text: element.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2173]:
            - text: In addition to an accessible name, the label provides a larger 'hit' area for mouse and touch screen users to click on or touch. By pairing a
            - code [ref=f2e2174]: <label>
            - text: with an
            - code [ref=f2e2175]: <input>
            - text: ", clicking on either one will focus the"
            - code [ref=f2e2176]: <input>
            - text: . If you use plain text to "label" your input, this won't happen. Having the prompt part of the activation area for the input is helpful for people with motor control conditions.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2177]: As web developers, it's important that we never assume that people will know all the things that we know. The diversity of people using the web—and by extension your website—practically guarantees that some of your site's visitors will have some variation in thought processes and/or circumstances that leads them to interpret your forms very differently from you without clear and properly-presented labels.
          - heading "Placeholders are not accessible" [level=4] [ref=f2e2178]
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2179]:
            - text: The
            - link [ref=f2e2180] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#placeholder"
              - code [ref=f2e2181]: placeholder
            - text: attribute lets you specify text that appears within the
            - code [ref=f2e2182]: <input>
            - text: element's content area itself when it is empty. The placeholder should never be required to understand your forms. It is not a label, and should not be used as a substitute, because it isn't. The placeholder is used to provide a hint as to what an inputted value should look like, not an explanation or prompt.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2183]:
            - text: Not only is the placeholder not accessible to screen readers, but once the user enters any text into the form control, or if the form control already has a value, the placeholder disappears. Browsers with automatic page translation features may skip over attributes when translating, meaning the
            - code [ref=f2e2184]: placeholder
            - text: may not get translated.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2186]:
            - strong [ref=f2e2187]: "Note:"
            - text: Don't use the
            - link [ref=f2e2188] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#placeholder"
              - code [ref=f2e2189]: placeholder
            - text: attribute if you can avoid it. If you need to label an
            - code [ref=f2e2190]: <input>
            - text: element, use the
            - link [ref=f2e2191] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/label
              - code [ref=f2e2192]: <label>
            - text: element.
        - region [ref=f2e2193]:
          - heading [level=3] [ref=f2e2194]:
            - link "Client-side validation" [ref=f2e2195] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#client-side_validation"
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2197]:
            - strong [ref=f2e2198]: "Warning:"
            - text: Client-side validation is useful, but it does
            - emphasis [ref=f2e2199]: not
            - text: guarantee that the server will receive valid data. If the data must be in a specific format,
            - emphasis [ref=f2e2200]: always
            - text: verify it also on the server-side, and return a
            - link [ref=f2e2201] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status/400
              - code [ref=f2e2202]: "400"
              - text: HTTP response
            - text: if the format is invalid.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2203]:
            - text: In addition to using CSS to style inputs based on the
            - link [ref=f2e2204] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Selectors/:valid
              - code [ref=f2e2205]: :valid
            - text: or
            - link [ref=f2e2206] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: /en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Selectors/:invalid
              - code [ref=f2e2207]: :invalid
            - text: UI states based on the current state of each input, as noted in the
            - link "UI pseudo-classes" [ref=f2e2208] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#ui_pseudo-classes"
            - text: section above, the browser provides for client-side validation on (attempted) form submission. On form submission, if there is a form control that fails constraint validation, supporting browsers will display an error message on the first invalid form control; displaying a default message based on the error type, or a message set by you.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2209]:
            - text: Some input types and other attributes place limits on what values are valid for a given input. For example,
            - code [ref=f2e2210]: <input type="number" min="2" max="10" step="2">
            - text: means only the number 2, 4, 6, 8, or 10 are valid. Several errors could occur, including a
            - code [ref=f2e2211]: rangeUnderflow
            - text: error if the value is less than 2,
            - code [ref=f2e2212]: rangeOverflow
            - text: if greater than 10,
            - code [ref=f2e2213]: stepMismatch
            - text: if the value is a number between 2 and 10, but not an even integer (does not match the requirements of the
            - code [ref=f2e2214]: step
            - text: attribute), or
            - code [ref=f2e2215]: typeMismatch
            - text: if the value is not a number.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2216]:
            - text: For the input types whose domain of possible values is periodic (that is, at the highest possible value, the values wrap back around to the beginning rather than ending), it's possible for the values of the
            - link [ref=f2e2217] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#max"
              - code [ref=f2e2218]: max
            - text: and
            - link [ref=f2e2219] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#min"
              - code [ref=f2e2220]: min
            - text: properties to be reversed, which indicates that the range of permitted values starts at
            - code [ref=f2e2221]: min
            - text: ", wraps around to the lowest possible value, then continues on until"
            - code [ref=f2e2222]: max
            - text: "is reached. This is particularly useful for dates and times, such as when you want to allow the range to be from 8 PM to 8 AM:"
          - generic [ref=f2e2224]:

          - paragraph [ref=f2e2374]:

            - code [ref=f2e2375]: "null"
            - text: ), the form will be prevented from being submitted. If there is no custom error message, and none of the other properties return true,
            - code [ref=f2e2376]: valid
            - text: will be true, and the form can be submitted.
          - generic [ref=f2e2378]:

          - paragraph [ref=f2e2387]:

            - code [ref=f2e2434]: "const nameInput = document.querySelector(\"input\"); nameInput.addEventListener(\"input\", () => { nameInput.setCustomValidity(\"\"); nameInput.checkValidity(); }); nameInput.addEventListener(\"invalid\", () => { if (nameInput.value === \"\") { nameInput.setCustomValidity(\"Enter your username!\"); } else { nameInput.setCustomValidity( \"Usernames can only contain upper and lowercase letters. Try again!\", ); } });"

          - paragraph [ref=f2e2441]: "In brief:"
          - list [ref=f2e2442]:
            - listitem [ref=f2e2443]:
              - text: We check the valid state of the input element every time its value is changed by running the
              - code [ref=f2e2444]: checkValidity()
              - text: method via the
              - code [ref=f2e2445]: input
              - text: event handler.
            - listitem [ref=f2e2446]:
              - text: If the value is invalid, an
              - code [ref=f2e2447]: invalid
              - text: event is raised, and the
              - code [ref=f2e2448]: invalid
              - text: event handler function is run. Inside this function we work out whether the value is invalid because it is empty, or because it doesn't match the pattern, using an
              - code [ref=f2e2449]: if ()
              - text: block, and set a custom validity error message.
            - listitem [ref=f2e2450]: As a result, if the input value is invalid when the submit button is pressed, one of the custom error messages will be shown.
            - listitem [ref=f2e2451]:
              - text: If it is valid, it will submit as you'd expect. For this to happen, the custom validity has to be canceled, by invoking
              - code [ref=f2e2452]: setCustomValidity()
              - text: with an empty string value. We therefore do this every time the
              - code [ref=f2e2453]: input
              - text: event is raised. If you don't do this, and a custom validity was previously set, the input will register as invalid, even if it currently contains a valid value on submission.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2455]:
            - strong [ref=f2e2456]: "Note:"
            - text: Always validate input constraints both client side and server side. Constraint validation doesn't remove the need for validation on the
            - emphasis [ref=f2e2457]: server side
            - text: . Invalid values can still be sent by older browsers or by bad actors.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2459]:
            - strong [ref=f2e2460]: "Note:"
            - text: Firefox supported a proprietary error attribute —
            - code [ref=f2e2461]: x-moz-errormessage
            - text: — for many versions, which allowed you set custom error messages in a similar way. This has been removed as of version 66 (see
            - link "Firefox bug 1513890 (external)" [ref=f2e2462] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: https://bugzil.la/1513890
            - text: ).
        - region [ref=f2e2463]:
          - heading [level=3] [ref=f2e2464]:
            - link "Localization" [ref=f2e2465] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#localization"
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2466]:
            - text: The allowed inputs for certain
            - code [ref=f2e2467]: <input>
            - text: types depend on the locale. In some locales, 1,000.00 is a valid number, while in other locales the valid way to enter this number is 1.000,00.
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2468]:
            - text: Firefox uses the following heuristics to determine the locale to validate the user's input (at least for
            - code [ref=f2e2469]: type="number"
            - text: "):"
          - list [ref=f2e2470]:
            - listitem [ref=f2e2471]:
              - text: Try the language specified by a
              - code [ref=f2e2472]: lang
              - text: /
              - code [ref=f2e2473]: xml:lang
              - text: attribute on the element or any of its parents.
            - listitem [ref=f2e2474]:
              - text: Try the language specified by any
              - code [ref=f2e2475]: Content-Language
              - text: HTTP header. Or,
            - listitem [ref=f2e2476]: If none specified, use the browser's locale.
        - region [ref=f2e2477]:
          - heading [level=2] [ref=f2e2478]:
            - link "Accessibility" [ref=f2e2479] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#accessibility"
        - region [ref=f2e2480]:
          - heading [level=3] [ref=f2e2481]:
            - link "Labels" [ref=f2e2482] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#labels_2"
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2483]:
            - text: When including inputs, it is an accessibility requirement to add labels alongside. This is needed so those who use assistive technologies can tell what the input is for. Also, clicking or touching a label gives focus to the label's associated form control. This improves the accessibility and usability for sighted users, increases the area a user can click or touch to activate the form control. This is especially useful (and even needed) for radio buttons and checkboxes, which are tiny. For more information about labels in general see
            - link "Labels" [ref=f2e2484] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: "#labels"
            - text: .
          - paragraph [ref=f2e2485]:
            - text: The following is an example of how to associate the
            - code [ref=f2e2486]: <label>
            - text: with an
            - code [ref=f2e2487]: <input>
            - text: element in the above style. You need to give the
            - code [ref=f2e2488]: <input>
            - text: an
            - code [ref=f2e2489]: id
            - text: attribute. The
            - code [ref=f2e2490]: <label>
            - text: then needs a
            - code [ref=f2e2491]: for
            - text: attribute whose value is the same as the input's
            - code [ref=f2e2492]: id
            - text: .

          - paragraph [ref=f2e2516]:
            - text: Interactive elements such as form input should provide an area large enough that it is easy to activate them. This helps a variety of people, including people with motor control issues and people using non-precise forms of input such as a stylus or fingers. A minimum interactive size of 44×44
            - link "CSS pixels (external)" [ref=f2e2517] [cursor=pointer]:
              - /url: https://w3c.github.io/wcag/guidelines/22/#dfn-css-pixels
            - text: is recommended.
